result:
I fixed both override problems. The existing suite passes (616 tests) and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. I didn't add tests for the new behaviour, so the switch-off and rejection cases are untested.

**Switching an override off**
- `updateOrg` in `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts` merged the incoming override list into the stored one, so nothing could ever be removed. It now replaces the list when a patch includes it and leaves it alone when the patch doesn't.
- `updateOrganization` in `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` now drops `enabledFlagOverrides` from general settings updates. The schema defaults that field to `[]`, so without this an ordinary settings save would have wiped every override. Overrides are now changed only through `toggleFlag`, which passes the full set, so switching one off removes just that one and switching it on again works.

**Non-overridable features**
- `toggleFlag` in `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` had an exception that let plan-based flags through the overridable check. Any request to switch on a non-overridable flag is now rejected with an error before anything is stored.
- `toggle-flag.ts` skipped the write when the flag was already enabled, which would have let `command_palette` (always on) report success on a switch-on request. That shortcut no longer applies to switch-on requests for non-overridable flags, so they reach the service and get rejected.
- `isEnabled` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` now honors an override only for flags declared overridable. A non-overridable override already stored in a workspace has no effect, and the flag is decided by its own rule. Overridable features work with overrides as before.

I left switch-off requests for non-overridable flags allowed, since they can only remove a stale stored override.
